desc: Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad is the largest stadium in the world by seating capacity, holding 132,000 spectators. Originally built in 1983 as the Motera Stadium, it underwent a massive reconstruction completed in 2020. The stadium features a distinctive elliptical shape with 11 pitches and an indoor cricket academy. It hosts international cricket matches including Tests, ODIs, and T20Is. The stadium is the home ground of the Gujarat Titans in the Indian Premier League and has hosted Day-Night Test matches. It is named after the 14th Prime Minister of India.

desc: Eden Gardens is a historic cricket stadium in Kolkata, established in 1864. It is the oldest cricket stadium in India and one of the most iconic cricket venues in the world. With a seating capacity of 68,000, it is the second-largest cricket stadium in India. Known for its passionate crowds and rich history, Eden Gardens has hosted numerous historic matches including World Cup and T20 World Cup finals. It is the home ground of the Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL and the Bengal cricket team. The stadium underwent major renovations in 2017.
fact: It is the oldest cricket stadium in India, established in 1864 · With 68,000 capacity, it is India's second-largest cricket stadium · It is the home ground of Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL · It has hosted numerous historic World Cup and T20 World Cup finals

desc: Wankhede Stadium is a premier cricket stadium located in Churchgate, Mumbai. Built in 1974, it has a seating capacity of 33,108. The stadium is famous for hosting the 2011 Cricket World Cup final, where India defeated Sri Lanka to win the title. It is the home ground of the Mumbai Indians in the IPL and the Mumbai cricket team. The stadium features a distinctive curved stands structure and modern facilities including floodlights for day-night matches. It is known for its energetic crowd and has been the venue for several memorable Test and ODI matches.
fact: It hosted the 2011 Cricket World Cup final where India won the title · Built in 1974, it has a capacity of 33,108 · It is the home ground of Mumbai Indians in the IPL · It is located in Churchgate, Mumbai near the Marine Drive

desc: M. A. Chidambaram Stadium, popularly known as Chepauk Stadium, is a historic cricket venue in Chennai. Established in 1916, it is the second-oldest cricket stadium in India after Eden Gardens. The stadium has a seating capacity of 38,000 and retains its historic red-brick architecture. It is the home ground of the Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, one of the most successful teams in the league. The stadium is known for its spin-friendly pitch and passionate crowd. It has hosted numerous historic Test matches featuring legendary Indian spinners.
fact: It is the second-oldest cricket stadium in India, established in 1916 · It is the home ground of Chennai Super Kings in the IPL · It is known for its spin-friendly pitch and historic red-brick architecture · It has hosted historic Test matches featuring legendary Indian spinners

desc: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium is a cricket stadium located in the Cubbon Road area of Bengaluru. Established in 1969, it has a seating capacity of 33,800. The stadium is the home ground of the Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the IPL. It is known for its batting-friendly wicket, high-scoring matches, and vibrant crowd. The stadium was the first in India to install solar panels on its roof. It has hosted many historic matches including the 1996 Cricket World Cup and the 2012 Women's T20 World Cup. The Karnataka State Cricket Association is headquartered here.

desc: Salt Lake Stadium, also known as Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, is a multi-purpose stadium in Kolkata. It is one of the largest football stadiums in Asia with a seating capacity of 85,000. The stadium was built in 1984 and has hosted numerous international football matches and athletic events. It is the home ground of ATK Mohun Bagan in the Indian Super League and the East Bengal and Mohun Bagan clubs. The stadium features modern facilities including floodlights, electronic scoreboards, and synthetic track. It is the largest sporting venue in India by seating capacity.
